analysis.title: October 2026 Hedge Fund Recap
key_insights: Average Global L/S fund fell 3.1% in October vs MSCI AC World -1.6%, the 4th negative month of 2026 for Global L/S (after March -4.6%, July -1.8%, September -1.5%). It is the second month in a row that Global L/S lost more than the MSCI in a down tape.

Global L/S alpha eroded on both sides of the book: long alpha -3.2% and short alpha -1.3% for the month. The YTD long-short spread is +1.8% vs +7% through September. Long alpha is barely positive YTD at ~15bps, short alpha is +1.6% YTD vs +3.1% through September.

Return dispersion is wide. The 25th percentile Global L/S fund is down ~4.1% YTD, about 40% of Global L/S funds are flat to negative YTD, and the October spread between the 90th (+2.3%) and 10th (-7.9%) percentiles was ~10.2%.

HFs were net sellers of global equities via the long side in October, led by N. America, then APAC, Japan and Europe. Multi-Strat/Macro and Equity L/S strategies drove the selling, while Stat Arb/Quant flows were more muted.

Equity L/S funds have actively unwound ~9% of global gross exposure between late June and end of October, the largest active L/S de-grossing across global equities in the last decade. Including price impact it still falls short of the COVID drawdown (-30%) and the 2021-2022 period (~40%).
Global L/S ratio ex-Quants is 1.86x, in the 3rd percentile over 12 months and the 1st percentile over 5 years.

US L/S funds have actively cut N. America gross exposure by 6.6% since end of June. US L/S gross leverage ended October at 206% (3rd percentile on 12 months) and net leverage at 47% vs a 53% YTD average. Long alpha on US positions fell from ~10% YTD at the peak to +50bps, and US short alpha was negative in October.

In prior midterm election years HFs unwound gross into the midterms and re-grossed afterward. MS notes the lack of a PnL cushion calls into question whether HFs will follow that pattern into year-end.

HF net exposure to AI themes fell from ~47% of US net exposure at end of June to under 35% at end of October. HFs are underweight AI vs market cap weight (~35% of HF net portfolios vs ~36% of US equity market cap) for the first time since the trade took hold. MS says positioning risk cuts both ways: HFs could sell into weakness or chase a move higher.

HFs rotated away from Momentum, which fell 13.1% in the month, with net Momentum exposure at 12-month troughs. Shorts tilted toward low-quality and small-caps, leaving Quality and Size tilts near multi-year highs.

Russell 2000 short interest is above the 90th percentile across all three major HF cohorts, a consensus short. HFs unwound some shorts over the final ~7 sessions of October but remain among the most bearishly positioned in the last year, so the trade is susceptible to sharp moves higher.

Europe: HFs continued to cut gross exposure despite net exposure near 15Y+ lows and EU at under 15% of global gross. The EU Top 50 crowded long-short spread had its worst month in 10+ years at -7.9% (record prior was July at -7.6%), with both long and short alpha negative. That has happened eight times since 2016, three of them in 2026.

Europe themes: long selling in EU Oil Majors and EU HC Equipment, which sit near the top of their 12M net exposure ranges. Short covering lifted EU AI Disruption (+15.7% vs SXXP), EU Software (+13.1%) and EU High Short Interest (+3.7%). HFs covered shorts in Big 5 UK Banks, which lagged SXXP by ~15%.

Asia: L/S funds cut APAC gross at the largest active pace in a decade, with long selling concentrated in AI trades in Taiwan, Japan and Korea. HF net exposure to Japan, Korea and Taiwan fell from ~23% to 15% of global net exposure. Asia Semis (-21.2%) is now 6% of global net exposure, half its June peak of 13%.
Quant/Multi-Manager median Global fund lost ~49bps in October (YTD +89bps). Momentum cost ~14bps and Beta ~4bps because the cohort was long both factors at end of Q3.

By sector, the L/S spread was weakest in Info Tech (-8.5%, longs down ~14% in absolute terms, YTD tech spread +13.0%), with Materials strongest (+2.0%) and Cons Staples next (+1.5%). By region, APAC was -8.7% (Japan -10.6%), N. America -3.2%, Europe -2.8%, and LatAm +1.4%.

sector_views.rationale: Info Tech had the weakest L/S spread in October at -8.5%, with longs down ~14% in absolute terms. HFs sold AI longs in N. America and Asia.
Materials had the strongest L/S spread in October at +2.0%, driven by shorts falling 3.6% more than longs.

risk_factors: Lack of a PnL cushion may keep HFs from re-grossing into year-end as they did after prior midterm elections.
HFs remain sizable in AI names and could sell into further weakness.
A consensus short in the Russell 2000 is exposed to sharp upside moves.
Elevated return dispersion, with about 40% of Global L/S funds flat to negative YTD.
Crowded positions continue to be a source of losses in both Europe and Asia.
vol_and_positioning: US L/S gross leverage is 206% (3rd percentile on 12 months) and net leverage is 47% vs a 53% YTD average.
Global L/S ratio ex-Quants is 1.86x, 3rd percentile over 12 months and 1st percentile over 5 years.
Russell 2000 short interest is above the 90th percentile across all three major HF cohorts, a consensus short exposed to sharp upside moves.

HF net exposure to AI is under 35% of US net exposure vs ~36% of US market cap, the first underweight since the trade took hold. MS says this could produce selling into weakness or chasing into strength.
HF net Momentum exposure is at 12-month troughs after the Momentum factor fell 13.1% in October. Quality and Size tilts are near multi-year highs.
EU HF net exposure is near 15Y+ lows and EU is under 15% of global gross exposure. Asia Semis is 6% of global net exposure vs a 13% peak in June.
US gross leverage is 206%, Europe 172% and Asia 127%. Net leverage is US 47%, Europe 53% and Asia 55%.

tension_points.bull_case: HFs are now slightly underweight AI vs market cap (<35% of net vs ~36% of US market cap), so they would need to buy at a sharper clip to keep pace with a move higher.
tension_points.bear_case: AI names remain a material weight in portfolios and a key driver of PnL, so HFs could be quick to sell into further weakness.

tension_points.bull_case: In prior midterm election years HFs unwound gross into the midterms and then added to gross exposure after the event. US gross leverage is at 12-month troughs.
tension_points.bear_case: The lack of a PnL cushion calls into question whether HFs will be willing to deploy further risk into year-end.
